html:
The Congo Crisis was a period of turmoil in the Congo from just after independence on 30 June 1960 until Mobutu's coup in November 1965.

Days after independence the army mutinied against its Belgian officers, Belgian troops returned, and Katanga, rich in copper, broke away under Moïse Tshombe. Prime Minister Patrice Lumumba asked the United Nations for help, which sent a large force, its biggest operation until then.

Lumumba was deposed and murdered in Katanga in January 1961. The UN Secretary-General Dag Hammarskjöld died in a plane crash near Ndola in September 1961 on a peace mission. UN troops ended the Katanga secession in 1963, but the Simba rebellion followed. Mobutu seized power in 1965, with Western backing, as the Cold War reached Africa.
sum: The Congo Crisis was a period of turmoil in the Congo from just after independence on 30 June 1960 until Mobutu's coup in November 1965.
